$notYetAppliedOrdinals_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-09 against the canonical project's own applied-migration list. This field previously read [] — that was wrong: 0030 (CEO Notebook) and 0031 (Business Transformation intake) have never been applied, and both migration headers say so, so the registry disagreed with both production and the files it governs. 0048 (barberos), 0049 (transform_audit), 0050 (citext guard semantics forward-repair), 0051 (unknown-is-not-complete) and 0052 (barberos owned_website) were APPLIED to canonical production under CEO approval, each verified by a normalized schema+seed fingerprint identical to the local build. 0052 was applied 2026-09-10; its fingerprint over the four new tables, their constraints, policies, triggers, grants, the nine new functions, both new enums and the permission and capability rows matched local exactly (a0c31416669a57cc0e7a4fd542a7f62d), and the security advisor count was unchanged at 36. 0053 (the public read path for a published page -- the first anon-executable RPC in the platform) was APPLIED 2026-09-10 under CEO approval, fingerprint-identical to local on the first comparison (647ace45300930371f6d68e6b0b0b157), and the `site` edge function was deployed the same day -- the first deployed edge function in this platform. Security advisors went 36 -> 40: two new lints naming only the two intended anon-callable wrappers, each counted under both the anon and the authenticated SECURITY DEFINER lint. See docs/architecture-audit/hlvs-phase-11-2l-production-deployment/. 0054 (the discovery call -- what a shop says it runs, learned on the introductory phone call) was APPLIED 2026-09-11 under CEO approval. Fingerprint over transform_audit.discovery's columns, its four constraints, its policies, its trigger, its grants, the two new functions and the new permission row was identical local and production on the FIRST comparison: f015d345b71fac28f0ae26937a502af1. 0055 (the proposal document) was APPLIED 2026-09-11 under CEO approval. Fingerprint over the table's columns, its six check constraints, its policy, its four triggers, the eight new functions, the grants on all of them, the new enum and the seeded permission rows: aa0fe867d3c7e26a14c9458db7e6a759, identical local and production. It differed on the FIRST comparison in exactly one component -- the RLS policy -- for the SAME reason 0052 did: production renders the policy's citext literal as '...'::citext because `extensions` is on its search_path, while the local mirror renders '...'::extensions.citext. Same type, different printing; the fingerprint query now normalizes it in policy expressions as well as in function sources and argument lists. Beyond the schema comparison the honesty trigger was exercised AGAINST PRODUCTION and refused all four cases with the exact expected messages -- a deferred module, a planned module claimed as deliverable today, a module not in the catalog, and a document with no offer array -- leaving 0 rows behind. Security advisors unchanged at 40, the same 40 as before, none in transform_audit: the six new SECURITY DEFINER functions live in a schema that is not in the exposed API allow-list. 0056 (the BarberOS shop API -- the door that lets a shop operate its own page, since PostgREST exposes only `public` and every barberos write function was therefore unreachable from any application) was APPLIED 2026-09-13 under CEO approval. Fingerprint over the ten new functions, their identity arguments, results, volatility, security mode, search_path pinning and bodies, plus every grant on them, their comments, and the REACH the door actually opens (how many public barberos_* functions anon and authenticated may execute, how many are SECURITY DEFINER, and whether anon has USAGE on barberos): 13d44cfd5c1569fca2a3a3cd1a86c513, identical local and production on the FIRST comparison, all four components. Exercised against production rather than only inspected: a signed-in stranger -- a real JWT for a user who is a member of nothing -- gets [] from barberos_my_shops() and is refused saving, publishing and deleting with the underlying barberos function's own message. Reach confirmed on production: anon may execute 2 of the public barberos_* functions (0053's, unchanged), authenticated may execute 11, exactly 2 are SECURITY DEFINER (0053's), and anon still has no USAGE on schema barberos. SECURITY ADVISORS UNCHANGED AT 40: nine new externally callable functions added zero findings because they are SECURITY INVOKER. The first draft made them DEFINER, copying 0053's reasoning -- which is about anon, not authenticated -- and would have added nine. 0057 (the product map -- the catalog widened to the CEO's twelve-layer definition of BarberOS, with what each unbuilt module is waiting on and who can clear it) was APPLIED 2026-09-13 under CEO approval. Fingerprint over the table's columns, its constraints, the new enum, all sixteen capability rows (name, category, status, version, locked config keys, blocker and description) and the dependency graph: 3a8e907b6ca7f46976cee685f2d860a5. It differed on the first comparison in exactly one component -- the column list -- for the FOURTH time on the same cause: production renders citext columns as `citext` because `extensions` is on its search_path, the local mirror as `extensions.citext`. Same type, different printing (0050, 0052, 0055, now 0057); normalize it in EVERY component of any fingerprint by default. Both new constraints were exercised against production and refused all three cases: a blocked module marked shipped, a blocker with no owner, and a shipped module given a blocker. Production state: 16 capabilities, 7 waiting on an account only the CEO can open, 7 on engineering, 1 shipped (owned_website), 1 deferred (payments). No tables and no functions were added, so the security-advisor surface is unchanged by construction. 0058 (client_crm -- the client record: who the shop cuts, the cut that was actually given, and the rhythm they come back on) was APPLIED 2026-09-13 under CEO approval. It is the second of the CEO's twelve layers to ship and the module retention, marketing and the advisor are all measured against. Fingerprint over four tables' columns, their constraints, RLS policies and triggers, three new enums, thirteen functions with their bodies, volatility, security mode and search_path pinning, every grant and ACL, the indexes, and the seeded permission and capability rows: 8f1f258d441b6391697c17681204ce4a, identical local and production across all nine components. It differed on the FIRST comparison in exactly one component -- c_fns -- and the cause was mine, not the database's: while transcribing the apply I stripped the in-body comments from four functions (upsert_client, record_visit, client_rhythm, client_timeline), so prosrc diverged while every other property matched. Re-applied verbatim with `create or replace`, and the lesson is now a rule: STRIP NOTHING WHEN TRANSCRIBING A MIGRATION -- the fingerprint covers function bodies and will catch it, but only after the fact. Exercised against production rather than only inspected, inside a DO block that aborted so nothing was written: writing a client before the capability is enabled is refused 42501 by the gate trigger; a visit dated tomorrow, a guard length on a scissor top and a beard guard with no beard are each refused 23514 by check constraints; a visit filed against another shop's client is refused with 'client ... belongs to a different shop'; reading another shop's client is refused 42501; the rhythm reports typical_days NULL with basis 'not enough visits to know a rhythm' after two visits and 28 days after three; and the timeline reports $80.00 across 3 visits WITH 1 visit carrying no price. Afterwards clients, visits, tools, visit_tools and tenant_capabilities for client_crm all read 0. SECURITY ADVISORS UNCHANGED AT 40 (9 + 6 + 2 + 2 + 20 + 1), the same 40 as before: the four new tables carry RLS and policies, the seven new SECURITY DEFINER functions live in `barberos`, which is not in the exposed API allow-list, and the six public wrappers are SECURITY INVOKER. 0059 (booking -- the appointment book) is BUILT AND NOT APPLIED, and 59 is listed in notYetAppliedOrdinals above for exactly that reason: it awaits CEO approval like every other migration. Three things about it are worth reading before approving. (1) IT INSTALLS AN EXTENSION: btree_gist, into the `extensions` schema, because the no-double-booking rule is an EXCLUSION CONSTRAINT and btree_gist is what lets one gist index mix an equality column (the barber) with an overlap column (the time range). It is standard PostgreSQL contrib, is already available in the project, and installing it into `extensions` rather than `public` keeps the extension-in-public advisor count where it is. (2) IT CHANGES A LIVE TABLE: barberos.site_services is repointed from barberos.sites(tenant_id) to barberos.shops(tenant_id). The new key is strictly weaker -- every shop with a page is a shop -- so no existing row can be invalidated, and production holds exactly one site_services row today. Its capability gate now admits owned_website OR booking, and its RLS policy now asks the same question the shop record asks rather than 'can you see the page'. This is a modelling correction, stated as one: 0052 hung the service list off the web page, and a shop's services belong to the SHOP. Without it booking could not be sold without the website module, which would have broken the `starter` bundle (client_crm + booking + review_engine, no website). (3) IT REDEFINES public.barberos_my_shops() to add three keys to `can` -- manage_clients, take_bookings and manage_rota. The app reads a missing key as false, so this is additive for anything already deployed. manage_clients is a defect fix: 0058 shipped without it and the clients screen drew 'Add a client' for a viewer the database would then refuse.
